questions.prompt: Why is abrupt cessation not a universal safe strategy?
questions.answer: Some substance or medicine withdrawal can be medically dangerous.
questions.feedback: Identify the need for assessment without giving a cessation plan.

questions.prompt: Who should advise on prescribed benzodiazepine discontinuation?
questions.answer: A qualified medical professional, normally the prescribing clinician.

questions.prompt: What should serious acute symptoms prompt?
questions.feedback: Do not substitute a helpline or worksheet for emergency care.

questions.prompt: Is difficulty stopping a recreational activity equivalent to medical withdrawal risk?
questions.answer: No; categories, mechanisms and care requirements differ.
questions.feedback: Avoid generalising from a behavioural example.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer, formative only; use specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Recognises withdrawal-related referral boundaries and selects medical or emergency help without giving a discontinuation plan.
scoring.transfer: Complete the fictional support map capstone. Include one routine case, one impairment case and one withdrawal-related case. Explicitly distinguish immediate emergency response from non-emergency professional referral. Identify which decisions require medical expertise.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; never average away missing or safety-critical evidence. Quizzes cannot certify competence.
